condition: Blunt abdominal trauma in pregnancy (suspected placental abruption)
summary: 29-year-old woman at 30 weeks, restrained front passenger in a collision 45 min ago: abdominal pain, uterine tenderness and tightenings, small vaginal bleed, HR 110, BP 102/64 (booking 118/74); blood group O RhD negative.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Abdominal pain after car crash, 30 weeks pregnant
inputs.hpi: Front-seat passenger, lap-and-shoulder belt, in a 50 km/h frontal collision 45 minutes ago. Now lower abdominal pain, uterus feels tight, small amount of fresh vaginal bleeding. Baby moving less. Second pregnancy, uncomplicated so far. Blood group O RhD negative.

exam.abdomen: Seat-belt bruise across the lower abdomen. Uterus tender and firm, fundus consistent with 30 weeks, tightening palpably. Fetal heart 150/min on Doppler.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Blunt abdominal trauma in pregnancy (30 weeks) — suspected placental abruption
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Blunt abdominal trauma at 30 weeks with uterine tenderness, contractions and vaginal bleeding — placental abruption until proven otherwise. Left lateral tilt / manual uterine displacement, obstetric team now, CTG, Kleihauer and anti-D (RhD negative).

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE has no placental abruption; top 3: Acute cholecystitis, Blunt abdominal trauma, Splenic laceration. Symptom inference ranks ectopic pregnancy #1 at 30 weeks.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add a trauma-in-pregnancy protocol/branch (left lateral tilt or manual uterine displacement after 20 weeks, early obstetric team, CTG ≥4–6 h, Kleihauer and anti-D if RhD negative, abruption) triggered by pregnancy status + trauma mechanism, with O9A.2 prefixes.

mustExclude.note: A known 30-week pregnancy does not need a pregnancy test; the prompt should adapt.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No trauma-in-pregnancy content exists: O9A.213 maps to no protocol, PANE top is below 0.20, and the blunt-trauma protocol has no pregnancy branch; the pregnancy prompt only asks for a urine pregnancy test.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a trauma-in-pregnancy protocol/branch (left lateral tilt or manual uterine displacement after 20 weeks, early obstetric team, CTG ≥4–6 h, Kleihauer and anti-D if RhD negative, abruption) triggered by pregnancy status + trauma mechanism, with O9A.2 prefixes.

mustExclude.note: A PE or ACS antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to a haemorrhagic or non-thrombotic diagnosis. Reading the iOS source, DiagnosisRadiationEngine.radiate matches keywords by substring and would attach the ACS plan ("mi" inside "abdominal", "limb", "haemodynamically") or the PE plan ("pe" inside "suspected", "penetrating", "superficial") to this diagnosis — to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — trauma in pregnancy
guideline.section: Chapter 12: resuscitate the mother first; manual uterine displacement / left lateral tilt after ~20 weeks to relieve aortocaval compression; early obstetric consultation; fetal monitoring (cardiotocography) for at least 6 h after injury beyond viability; Kleihauer–Betke test and anti-D immunoglobulin for Rh-negative mothers; consider placental abruption; indicated imaging must not be withheld
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 12.

guideline.name: BSH guideline — use of anti-D immunoglobulin for the prevention of haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn
guideline.section: Potentially sensitising events after 20 weeks (including abdominal trauma) in RhD-negative women: anti-D immunoglobulin and a test of fetomaternal haemorrhage volume (e.g. Kleihauer)
guideline.citation: Qureshi H, Massey E, Kirwan D, et al. BCSH guideline for the use of anti-D immunoglobulin for the prevention of haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn. Transfus Med. 2014;24:8–20.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — initial assessment and management
guideline.section: Chapter 1: primary survey in order — control of exsanguinating external haemorrhage, airway with cervical spine restriction, breathing, circulation with haemorrhage control, disability, exposure (x/c-ABCDE); adjuncts (FAST, CXR, pelvic XR); resuscitation before definitive imaging in unstable patients
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 1.

rationale: Trauma in pregnancy: the mother is resuscitated first with left lateral tilt/manual uterine displacement, early obstetric involvement, CTG and Kleihauer/anti-D for an RhD-negative mother; abruption must be on the differential. ICD O9A.213 is the pregnancy-specific injury code.
